hook.text: A treasury agent puts thirty percent into a pool.
Then the session ends, and the agent forgets it ever happened.

product.text: Groundhog Vault is a treasury agent that remembers

setup.text: Two agents get the same capital,
the same decision logic, and the same market.
Only one of them can read Sibyl memory.

life1.text: Both allocate thirty percent to MoonPool.

destroy.text: an incident entity, an append-only event,
and a risk policy keyed by the risk signature,

life2.text: A fresh Groundhog session recalls the policy and
Memory preserved twelve thousand three hundred dollars.

evidence.text: The evidence view traces it end to end.
The MoonPool incident, the policy it produced,
and the fresh decision that policy changed.
Every recommendation points back to the loss that taught it.

walkthrough.text: Recall it by signature in a fresh session.

treasury.text: It works on a treasury's own history too.
Record a real incident, then evaluate a differently
named proposal in a brand new session.
and it cites the policy and the incident behind it.

base.text: The user signs that recommendation as a decision
receipt on Base Sepolia, linking the allocation
to hashes of its policy and source incident.
The agent never holds the wallet.

production.text: This is a simulation that never moves funds.
A deployed guardian would issue constrained proposals:
attached, and human approval before anything executes.

close.text: Do not pay for the same lesson twice.
